vignette: A 34-year-old client presents two weeks after the end of a long-term relationship. They report four weeks of low mood, waking at 3 a.m. most nights, a 12-pound unintentional weight loss, and difficulty concentrating at work. During intake they say quietly, "Some mornings I wonder what the point of getting up is." They have no prior counseling history and are not taking any medication.
question: What do you do FIRST?

options.text: Assess safety and suicidal ideation directly
Administer the PHQ-9 to quantify symptom severity
Begin cognitive restructuring around the breakup
Refer to a psychiatrist for a medication evaluation

rationale: A passive death wish stated in session is a safety signal, and safety assessment always precedes measurement, intervention, and referral. Screening tools, treatment, and consultation all remain appropriate — after risk has been directly evaluated.
